translation_notes: prefixes: prop->prop, res->res, dbo->dbo, DC->dc, DCTERMS->dcterms, DOAP->doap, FOAF->foaf, SKOS->skos, OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, VOID->void, XMLNS->xmlns, XSD->xsd

`res:` doubles as an ID factory in the original: `res+'sub_'+dsName+str(val[0])` builds a plain Python str consumed later by two different URIRef(...) calls, not a term construction on its own. Declared `@prefix res: <...> as RES .` so the string-building keeps using the Namespace object (RES) exactly as before, while every position that actually places a triple term uses the res: prefixed name instead of URIRef(res+'literal').

constant local parts (distribution, hasSentence, hasText, hasNamedEntity, numOfRelation, hasSubject, hasObject) became bare prefixed names (prop:hasSentence); the two data-driven ones (prop+key, dbo+remove_alphaNumeric(...)) became prop:{key} and dbo:{remove_alphaNumeric(nam_e[1])} -- the 0.4.0 instantiated local part, safe here since key and the sanitised entity type never contain a space or slash.

missing module-level bindings (relation, dsName, sent_counter, ne_counter, info, subject_dict, object_dict) restored identically in original.py and translated.ldpy as a minimal fixture, since the region is a bare script fragment (kind: statement) rather than a function; validate.py is a context shim reproducing only the four functions the region calls, subset of V1/validate.py at the pinned commit.
one @graph g at the top designates the receiver for the whole loop body; each .add() becomes exactly one +{ } at its original nesting depth, including inside the deeply nested if/elif/else branches.

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `dc:`, `dcterms:`, `doap:`, `foaf:`, `skos:`, `owl:`, `rdf:`, `void:`, `xmlns:`, `xsd:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

repair.driver: Second run 'extended': the driver replaces the fixture block (info, subject_dict, object_dict) of both artefacts, textually and identically, with one that keeps the two existing entries and adds two in the repository's real shape (int counters 0 and 1 keyed by surface text, tokenize dicts with int counts including 0 and a bool direction, numOfRelation 0): texts 'Apollo 11'/'Route 66' take both containsNumber branches, '...'/'' both check_type branches; several non-entity keys reach prop:{key}. The artefacts are run from a temporary copy so original.py and translated.ldpy stay untouched (their metrics too); one combined verdict.
mutants_killed: rdfs:label -> rdfs:comment in each of the four branches
subject containsNumber label computed as in else (remove_alphaNumeric)
repair.remaining: Only the wrong-construction question of the triage (Literal(..., lang=)/Literal(..., datatype=)/URIRef(...) kept as interpolations instead of language/typed literals and f<...>): not handled by the repair.

credit_correction.what: unused prefix declarations dropped from translated.ldpy

optimization_notes: optimized.py: URIRef(prop+'x') becomes prop.x, URIRef(prop+key) prop[key] and URIRef(dbo+...) dbo[...] (remove_alphaNumeric returns a str; the sentence keys are str in the repository, where prop[key] would no longer raise on a non-str key); each run of adds becomes one `g += [...]`; the two unused enumerate indexes go (`for val in info`, `for v in val[2]`); `x = x + 1` becomes `x += 1`; each three-branch containsNumber/check_type/else label becomes one conditional expression (same short-circuit order) bound to subject_label / object_label, then one batch of two triples. The module-level names the driver compares (sent_id, ne_id, sub_id, obj_id, subject_string, object_string, the counters) keep their values.

A raising term (remove_alphaNumeric(None) when returnValue finds nothing) now raises before the batch it belongs to is written, where the original had written the hasSubject/hasObject or hasNamedEntity triple first: the script dies either way, as with the translation's +{ }.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g`, one `+{ }` per batch (`;` on the shared entity subject); Literal(x, datatype=XSD.y) becomes the typed literal `{x}^^{XSD.y}` and Literal(x, lang='en') the language literal `{x}@en` (both transpile to the same Literal call); prop.x, prop[key] and dbo[...] become prop:x, prop:{key} and dbo:{...}. No exception to the symmetry.
header_optimization_notes: Python: DC, DCTERMS, DOAP, FOAF, SKOS, OWL, VOID and XMLNS go from rdflib.namespace; is_date, clean_sentences and wikidata_id_toText go from the shim import. The fixture block stays byte for byte (the driver substitutes it textually).

LD Python: the same, plus RDF, RDFS, Literal and Namespace (the islands write a, rdfs:, the literals and the prefixes); the four @prefix lines stay: prop:, dbo:, rdfs: are written as prefixed names, and res: carries the RES Namespace object the ids are built from.
